extraAngles.prompt: THE MONOGRAPHS READ ONLY BY RELAY OR NOT AT ALL: Colin Manlove, Science Fiction: Ten Explorations (1986), the BotNS chapter — the earliest sustained close reading of the prose; Brian Attebery, Strategies of Fantasy (1992) on BotNS; John Clute, Strokes (1988) — the collected BotNS reviews; Peter Wright, Attending Daedalus (2003) direct (Internet Archive borrow + search-inside for 'suggestive rather than definitive', 'narratological sleight of hand', 'first misinterpreted narrative'); Joan Gordon, Gene Wolfe (Starmont 1986) — 498 KB of two-column OCR is on disk at prose-research/wolfe-raw/gw-gordon-1986.txt, unread: split the columns and read it; Robert Borski, Solar Labyrinth (2004) and The Long and the Short of It (2006); Andre-Driussi, Lexicon Urthus introduction; Aramini, Between Light and Shadow (2015) introduction; the SFS reviews via JSTOR (DOI 10.1525/sfs.32.1.0212 and the 1987 review of Gordon) or the Wayback id_ capture of the old depauw.edu/sfs paths; Logos 2015 'Art and Allegory', Critical Quarterly 2020 'Time After Time', the Liverpool UP Shadows of the New Sun chapters via OpenAlex/Crossref → Unpaywall → scholar.archive.org. Google Books snippet search for the relayed phrases where a borrow fails.

CLOSE READING, CONTINUED where the first finder stopped: the Urth-list close reading from chapter III onward (the October and November 2006 thread indexes are on disk: prose-research/wolfe-close-raw/t-2006-October.html, t-2006-November.html); Jo Walton's Reactor/Tor.com rereads (Peace, The Fifth Head of Cerberus, Soldier of the Mist; collected in What Makes This Book So Great, 2014); Michael Dirda (Washington Post) and Gary K. Wolfe (Locus) reviews; the Alzabo Soup and ReReading Wolfe episode transcripts via yt-dlp --write-auto-sub --skip-download (the saved caption URLs expired; regenerate); r/genewolfe top threads from the saved search JSON on disk; the cwhowell.com 'Dark Souls of Books', donbeck substack 'Structure of the New Sun', scatterings1976 and lofkin pages via the Wayback CDX API to recover the slug then the id_ capture. A quoted Wolfe SENTENCE analysed at sentence level outweighs any verdict.

regradeNotes: Apply the r4 standard to the kept set (the critic's §5): [2] and [4] — 'the puzzles are meant to be solved' and the cowboys/knights/spaceship enumeration are Jordan's QUESTION adopted by assent, not Wolfe's sentence → PARTIAL on the attribution limb (the [331] defect); [10] — the denial is singular ('The book') where the claim generalises → PARTIAL (the [7] defect); [17] and [228] — 'It's almost that it has to be' is softer than 'must be' → PARTIAL (the [0] defect); [358] — the page hedges with 'perhaps', the claim drops it → PARTIAL; [45] — 'people giving testimony at a trial', not 'adult witnesses'; the child/adult contrast is the question's frame → PARTIAL; [211] — the printed words 'a prison, a pleasure garden, and a tomb' exist only in the verifier's note, the row's quote is a different clause and trueWording is empty → PARTIAL until re-pointed; [380] — VERIFIED as 'a MetaFilter reader attributes to Wolfe …', but note 'ATTRIBUTED, no primary' so the section stops using it as Wolfe's own; [419] — Lee relaying unspecified comments → PARTIAL (no primary); [243] — Wikipedia's unattributed editorial synthesis is not a distinct source → PARTIAL; [147] — Price reporting a private conversation → note 'private conversation, sole basis with [41]'; [364] — the relayer is Mark R. Kelly, not Gordon (a misattribution in two places) → note it. Trim [174] (13 words) and [326] (13 words) to twelve. Every trueWording you write is at most twelve words; 223 kept rows exceed it — note 'fullSentence: trim before any copy' on each you touch.
synthNotes: Carry every finder-level BLOCKED / 404 into the coverage table as its own column (about a dozen: SFS #95 and 14.1, Logos 2015, Critical Quarterly 2020, the Cambridge Core intro, the image-only 2005 PDF, Roberts, the New Yorker, cwhowell, donbeck, lists.urth.net live, scatterings, fabulist-5hc, sffrd, lofkin, the 0-byte Gale review) so the zeroes stop reading as clean. Single-speaker features: 10 (all three 'sources' are Wolfe relayed), 16 (Wowra carries the whole feature; and the rule generalises an amnesiac's folk etymology to a settlement naming its land — a step no source takes), 4 (one speaker), 14 — say so. Reconcile: feature 10 ('no trace is repeated') against Aramini [142]/[145] (repetition is the signalling mechanism; late Wolfe repeats less) — Wolfe's 'once' is about clues to the puzzle, Aramini's repetition about world-facts; feature 1 (New Sun diction, real old words) against feature 36 (imitate the later Wolfe) — say which Wolfe's diction; feature 5 (the floor plan as law) against [37] (research while writing; the plan was drawn mid-draft); feature 13 (no feelings in the record) against Wolfe [31] (the first-person narrator may comment; only the AUTHOR's comment is ruinous) — the section forbids what Wolfe permits; feature 12 sides with the minority (omission only) against Gerwel, Auerbach, Gladstone, Gaiman and Wolfe's own [44] — either a DESIGN CHOICE stated on the DM page or rewritten; feature 3/32 (short, level) against Holland, Gevers, Kelly, Tree Slices — resolved by date through ONE source (Aramini [141]) with no measurement: if the measure angle landed, its numbers decide; merge or distinguish features 8 and 24 (same rows); feature 9's hazard ('a dossier that hides its central fact from every reader has failed') rests on [419] and a relay of Wright — no primary; feature 7's outsider-hand exception is ruled out by fiat while feature 15 makes the dossier 'a translation by a later hand' — decide whether the later hand may gloss. If the le-guin angle landed, Le Guin gets her own feature. Trim [174] in the partial table. The DM page cites book, chapter and page; never copy a trueWording over twelve words (223 kept rows are flagged fullSentence).
